dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Lorraine. I know it's Sunday afternoon, so you've reached the line they keep open outside regular City Hall hours. How can I help?
Hello, yes. Thank you for pick up. My name is Sofia Vieira. I call because of drain on my corner. [pause] I know City Hall is closed today, so I use this number.
That's right, this is the one to use on a weekend. Sofia, did I get that right? Sofia Vieira?
Yes, Vieira. V-I-E-I-R-A.
Got it. And what's going on with the drain?

The catch basin at the corner, it is clogged with leaf. Many, many leaf, all wet and stuck on top. After the nor'easter yesterday, the water cannot go down, so it come back up and go into my driveway. Friday and Saturday it rain so hard. Now the driveway still have puddle.
Okay, so the storm drain at the corner is packed with leaves, and the water is backing up into your driveway. Is that right?
Yes, exactly. And it is not only this storm. My neighbor tell me it happen every big rain. Every time. So I think, nobody clean it, or not enough.
I see. So your neighbor says this is a regular thing at that corner.
Yes. Every big rain, he say. I am frustrated, because I have my business, and customer need to come in by the driveway. Yesterday they cannot park, there is water all over.
That's no good, especially the day after a storm. Let me get the location down. What's the street, and what's the nearest cross street to that corner?
Um. I prefer not to say my address on the phone. But the corner, it is where the two street meet, with the big maple tree. The drain is on the side near the stop sign.
Okay. Without an address it's harder for the crew to find it. Could you give me just the two streets that cross at that corner? That wouldn't be your house number.
[pause] Hmm. Let me think. I will give the cross streets, but I would like you to call me back if crew need more. My number is four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-seven-one.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-seven-one. Perfect, I have that. And the streets?
[line breaks up] ...sorry, the phone is on speaker, I am knitting, so my hand are busy. You can hear the needle, click click, sorry.
Oh, I can barely hear it, you're fine. Go ahead with the streets whenever you're ready.
Okay. It is Bellevue Avenue and Narragansett Avenue. The corner by the stop sign, northeast side.
Bellevue and Narragansett, northeast corner by the stop sign, catch basin clogged with leaves, water backing into a driveway. Did I get all that?
Yes, you get all. Thank you. Please, I ask that the drain be clean. Not only look at it. Clean it, so the water can go down.

Understood, you're asking for the basin to be cleaned out. I'll put that in as a request for the crew with your number on it. Is the water in the driveway still standing right now, or is it going down?
It is going down slow. Still there is puddle, maybe this deep, like my hand. The driveway is not safe to walk, a little.

Okay, I'll note that it's still holding water. Crews are stretched thin right after a storm, so cleanouts like this get worked in as they can, probably early in the week. Someone may call you at that number if they need anything.
Early in the week. Okay. But I hope it is not same like before. My neighbor say he call before and nothing happen. I do not want to wait again for next rain.
I hear you. I'll mention in the notes that neighbors report it backs up in every heavy rain, so whoever picks it up knows it's a repeat spot, not a one-time thing.
Yes, please write like that. Every heavy rain. That is important.
Written down. Every heavy rain, leaves on the grate, water into the driveway. Anything else you want on it?
No, that is all. Thank you for your patience, Lorraine. I am sorry my English is slow.
Your English is fine, you were very clear. Have a good rest of your Sunday, Sofia.
You too. Goodbye.
